text.p: Italian debt markets joined the general race higher in the wake of U.S. inflation and retail sales data which diminished expectations of an imminent U.S. rate rise, traders said.

"The markets are positive because the U.S. numbers were good. People changed their minds and decided there'll be no rate hike at the next FOMC meeting. Every two weeks people seem to change their minds," a broker at a London-based bank commented.
The February 2006 BTp, in response to the data, charged up 55 basis points to 102.99, but only managed to wrench the spread over 10-year Btps in by one basis point to 300 bps.

The December future on LIFFE climbed 66 basis points to 117.45, with support at the previous 117.00 resistance level of the earlier part of the session and current resistance set at the range top of 118.00.

At home, there was little news to goad the market into action on things domestic. The market is waiting to hear more about the 1997 budget package being put together currently and how it will be received in parliament.
The lira continued relatively steady at 1,010.85/1.25 per mark. --Charlotte Cooper, Milan bureau +392 66129507
